title: Restore only validated associated operational scope
statement: The Work records Module shall restore only validated associated operational scope through its typed maintenance boundary, preserving actual scope, source meaning and safe failure.

what.problem: Loss of a local operational store can erase resumption context; an apparently successful restore can silently omit evidence or renew old judgments.
what.desired_outcome: An authorized participant can recover the declared retained work and identify every limitation before relying on it.

why.rationale: SR-075 requires operational preservation; MOD-011 owns the associated store and maintenance activation, while MOD-010 owns admission and result presentation.

stakeholders: Project maintainers and authorized agents relying on retained operational work

conditions: An actor explicitly selects the supported maintenance task, scope, source expectations and destination.

contexts: MOD-011 through IF-003, invoked by MOD-010 through IF-004; engineering definitions remain repository-owned.

how.approach: Use the reviewed MOD-011 maintenance contract: coherent staged scope, explicit project/schema/integrity checks, exclusive activation and attributable recovery outcomes.

how_much.scope: Selected retained supported records and payloads only; no silent merge, universal history retention, source deletion or renewed engineering approval.

acceptance_criteria: With the original store unavailable and a valid complete backup accessible, restore reproduces the selected records, finding dispositions, subjects and revisions, decisions, provenance and required artifact content in the declared project scope.

Wrong-project input, unsupported interpretation, corrupted content or missing required artifacts is rejected before destination activation; source backup and unrelated destination content remain unchanged.

Restored reviews and verification results retain their original subject identities and applicability; neither restoration nor a different current engineering revision renews approval or evidence freshness.

An occupied or changed destination causes an explicit conflict unless a separately authorized safe replacement is supported; restoration never silently merges divergent histories or overwrites newer work.
An interrupted restoration exposes no partially restored state as complete or ready for resumption; retry identifies the actual destination state and preserves existing usable content.
When no usable backup exists, restoration reports unavailable and does not initialize an empty history as successful recovery.
The public maintenance contract identifies preview versus execution, current expectations and actual effects; interrupted activation remains fenced until explicitly reconciled.
assumptions: Required retained source material and supported interpretation information are accessible; failure of that premise is reported explicitly.
constraints: Historical subject/revision provenance remains stable; restoring operational state creates a fresh store incarnation so old mutation tokens cannot be replayed.

sources.basis: Reconcile the existing reviewed maintenance responsibility with explicit REM allocation. This allocation is design intent, not execution or satisfaction evidence.
